name: r3a1-related-denial-admitted-and-audited
description: R3a-1 Outcome 2 negative control for the canonical `knowvault_related` workspace tool: a call by a principal without the workspace right must answer the existing content-free denial (no relation content, no excerpt, no address, no workspace-id echo) and must record admission before data and its classed denial outcome through the same authorized relation-source the production Evidence-graph read composes. internal/platform/workspaceapi/mcp_related.go's mcpRelatedToolCall dispatches the authorized EvidenceRelated source and then maps its error to the content-free -32004 `workspace relations not found`. Weakening the denial guard `if err != nil` to `if err == nil` (keeping the same `writeMCPError`/`return` block verbatim so the mutated file still reads `err` and keeps its brace balance) makes a denied non-member call fall through to the success projection with an empty relation page and `isError: false` instead of the existing -32004 refusal. Weakening the denial mapping from `-32004`/`workspace relations not found` to the generic `-32000`/`service unavailable` replaces the existing content-free denial with the wrong refusal. Both mutants compile and are killed behaviourally by internal/platform/workspaceapi/mcp_related_test.go TestMCPRelatedAdmissionBeforeData, which requires the -32004 refusal with no leaked relation content or workspace id and the `admission,denied` relation-source order.
baseline_meaning: On the unmutated tree a `knowvault_related` call by a principal without the workspace right resolves the addressed object through the injected EvidenceRelated source (in production the authorized relation-source of the cross-source Evidence-graph capability, which returns one content-free evidence.ErrNotFound for a non-member, unknown or foreign workspace), so mcpRelatedToolCall emits the existing content-free -32004 `workspace relations not found` with no `relations` rows, no excerpt and no echo of the requested workspace id. The denied membership read is journalled through the shared R1 admission-before-data mechanism with the closed denial outcome class (TestMCPRelatedAdmissionBeforeData asserts the `admission,denied` relation-source order).
mutant_meaning: With the denial guard weakened to `if err == nil` a denied/foreign call skips the refusal and falls through to the success projection, which carries an empty relation page and `isError: false`; the same weakening also refuses served calls (whose error is nil) with -32004, so the unmutated green case turns red too. With the denial mapping weakened to -32000 the same denial is answered with the generic service-unavailable refusal instead of the existing content-free -32004. Both mutated files still read `err` and keep the -32004 branch referenced, so internal/platform/workspaceapi compiles and the failure is the behavioural TestMCPRelatedAdmissionBeforeData assertion (a denied `knowvault_related` call must return the existing denial and no content), not a build failure; each mutant is killed by the registered probe and not vacuous.
runner: tests/contracts/mutation-runner/main.go executes these cases from tests/contracts/mutation-registry.json under the GO_UNIT harness for the invariant entry `acceptance.r3a1.related.denial-admitted-and-audited`; the identical cases are committed both here and in the registry so the proof is pinned to the product guard.
